questions.passage: Like all species of baleen whales, the Antarctic minke whale feeds on tiny creatures known as krill by filtering water through bristlelike keratin structures called baleen plates. And while no one would call the Antarctic minke whale small—it can have a mass as high as 10,000 kg—it is one of the smaller whales and is much smaller than the bowhead whale, which can weigh a whopping 66,000 kg and consume as much as 19,800 kg of krill per day.
questions.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be concluded about krill consumption among Antarctic minke and bowhead whales?
options: The bowhead whale is able to eat more krill per day than the Antarctic minke whale is.
Both the Antarctic minke whale and the bowhead whale can eat as much as 19,800 kg of krill per day.
The quantities of krill consumed by bowhead whales have made it difficult for Antarctic minke whales to find sufficient food.
Most baleen whales include krill in their diet, but the Antarctic minke whale is less likely than the bowhead whale to do so.

Helena says to Vanya, "You are cultured and intelligent, Vanya, and you surely understand that the world is not destroyed by villains and conflagrations, but by hate and malice and all this spiteful tattling. It is your duty to make peace [with Professor Serebrakoff], and not to growl at everything."

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Epistolary novels are novels written primarily as a series of fictional documents, typically letters.
  • Sometimes, the documents are journal entries, newspaper clippings, and more.
  • Julie, or The New Heloise (1761) is an epistolary novel by French author Jean Jacques Rousseau.
  • It consists primarily of letters sent between a man and a woman living in a small French town.
  • Absolutely Normal Chaos (1990) is an epistolary novel by American author Sharon Creech.
  • It consists primarily of journal entries written by a student during her summer vacation.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two novels. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The French author Jean Jacques Rousseau and the American author Sharon Creech have written epistolary novels.
While Julie, or The New Heloise and Absolutely Normal Chaos are both epistolary novels, the former is composed primarily of letters and the latter of journal entries.
Some epistolary novels consist primarily of journal entries, but most, like Jean Jacques Rousseau’s Julie, or The New Heloise, consist primarily of letters.
Jean Jacques Rousseau’s Julie, or The New Heloise, and Sharon Creech’s Absolutely Normal Chaos demonstrate the variety of documents that can be used in epistolary novels.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • A lever is a simple machine consisting of a rigid beam and a fulcrum.
  • The fulcrum is the point about which the beam pivots.
  • The input force (effort) is the force applied to the lever.
  • The output force (load) is the force that the lever exerts on another object.
  • In first-class levers, the fulcrum is located between the effort and the load.
  • In second-class levers, the load is located between the effort and the fulcrum.
questions.question: The student wants to contrast first-class levers and second-class levers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In levers, the effort is the force applied to the lever; the load, in contrast, is the force that the lever exerts on another object.
In first-class and second-class levers, the fulcrum and the load are in different locations.
First-class levers are simple machines consisting of a rigid beam and a fulcrum, but then again, the same is true of second-class levers.
In first-class levers, the fulcrum is located between the effort and the load, but in second-class levers, the load is located between the effort and the fulcrum.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Most of the plant and bird species in Oahu, Hawaii, are non-native.
  • In a 2019 study, researchers wanted to know what role non-native birds play in dispersing plant seeds in Oahu.
  • Researchers catalogued plant seeds found in fecal samples from non-native birds.
  • Touchardia latifolia, a flowering shrub, was one of fifteen native species catalogued.
  • Hedychium gardnerianum, an herbaceous vine, was one of twenty-nine non-native species catalogued.
  • Researchers concluded that non-native birds play a vital role in dispersing the seeds of native and non-native plants.
questions.question: The student wants to contrast the two plants. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Oahu, Hawaii, seeds from Touchardia latifolia and Hedychium gardnerianum plants were found in the fecal samples of non-native birds.
The plants Touchardia latifolia and Hedychium gardnerianum can be found in Oahu, Hawaii.
Touchardia latifolia, a species of shrub, is native to Oahu, Hawaii, but Hedychium gardnerianum, a species of vine, is not.
Most plant species found in Oahu, Hawaii, like Hedychium gardnerianum, are non-native.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Body positions are a fundamental aspect of dance.
  • In Vaganova method ballet, there is a position for the dancer’s arms called first position.
  • In the position, both arms are rounded to roughly align the fingers with the navel.
  • In Royal Academy of Dance ballet, there is a position for the dancer’s arms called demi-seconde position.
  • In this position, both arms are out to the sides but angled downward.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize similarity between the two positions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: First position in Vaganova method ballet and demi-seconde position in Royal Academy of Dance ballet are both positions for the dancer’s arms.
Both first position and demi-seconde position are positions in Royal Academy of Dance ballet.
In first position, both arms are rounded to roughly align the fingers with the navel, in contrast to demi-seconde position, where both arms are out to the sides but angled downward.
In Vaganova method ballet, there are a number of positions, including first position.
